Class MarketSimulationEngine

java.lang.Object
com.leap.leaplaughlove.marketdata.simulation.MarketSimulationEngine
@Service public class MarketSimulationEngine extends Object
Simulates instrument prices using Geometric Brownian Motion, ticking every active instrument on a fixed schedule and publishing a PriceTickEvent per tick.

  • Field Details

    • START_ORDER

      public static final int START_ORDER
      Order of initialize() among ApplicationReadyEvent listeners: last. Seeding the state is what starts ticks flowing (the scheduled tick() is already running), so every tick consumer that loads a lookup on the same event must run before it - order those with TICK_CONSUMER_ORDER.
      See Also:

    • MarketSimulationEngine

      public MarketSimulationEngine(SimulatedInstrumentRepository instrumentRepository, PriceCandleRepository candleRepository, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher eventPublisher, @Value("${marketdata.simulation.tick-interval-ms:1000}") long tickIntervalMs, @Value("${marketdata.simulation.candle-bucket-seconds:60,300,3600,86400}") List<Integer> candleBucketSeconds)
      Creates a new MarketSimulationEngine with the given collaborators and tick interval.
      Parameters:
      instrumentRepository - repository used to look up active instruments at startup
      candleRepository - repository used to resume each instrument's last persisted price
      eventPublisher - publisher used to broadcast PriceTickEvents
      tickIntervalMs - the interval, in milliseconds, between simulation ticks
      candleBucketSeconds - the candle widths, in seconds, searched for the price to resume from

  • Method Details

    • initialize

      @EventListener(org.springframework.boot.context.event.ApplicationReadyEvent.class) @Order(2147483647) public void initialize()
      Seeds the simulation state for every active instrument once the application context is ready, resuming from the newest persisted candle close where one exists and falling back to the instrument's configured initial price otherwise.

      Resuming matters because this runs on every boot. Restarting each instrument at its seed price made the persisted series jump back to that price at every restart, so a chart drawn over the candle history showed a sawtooth no market movement produced. It is also what lets the historical backfill hand off continuously: the backfill's final close becomes the live feed's opening price.

    • tick

      @Scheduled(fixedRateString="${marketdata.simulation.tick-interval-ms:1000}") public void tick()
      Advances every active instrument's simulated price by one GBM step and publishes a PriceTickEvent for each.
